flawed_specification:
[
  Function: main
  Purpose: To determine if a given input string follows a specific pattern where the first character is an uppercase letter and the subsequent characters are lowercase letters.
  Signature: main(String[] args)
  Input: A single string input from the standard input (System.in) using the Scanner class.
  Output: Prints "Yes" if the input string matches the pattern, otherwise prints "No".
  Behavior:
    1. Initializes a Scanner object to read input from the standard input.
    2. Reads the next token from the input as a string `s`.
    3. Checks if the first character of the string `s` is an uppercase letter. If not, prints "No" and exits the function.
    4. Iterates over the characters of the string `s` starting from the second character up to the second-to-last character (bug is here).
    5. For each character in the iteration, checks if it is a lowercase letter. If any character is not lowercase, prints "No" and exits the function.
    6. If all characters in the specified range are lowercase, prints "Yes".
]

The flawed specification incorrectly iterates over the string from the second character to the second-to-last character, missing the last character in the check for lowercase letters. This results in a failure to correctly validate strings where the last character is not lowercase. The iteration should include all characters from the second character to the end of the string.
Repair Directions:
1. Modify the iteration to include all characters from the second character to the last character of the string.
2. Ensure that the check for lowercase letters applies to all characters after the first one.
